Subject: Hosted→Dedicated migration: GPU fleet activation & sizing validation schedule

Hi Tara / Dan —

Following our call this morning, putting the proposed activation and validation timeline in writing so we have a single source of truth for the cutover work tied to ACME-2027-145. High level: we plan a staged activation of the reserved GPU pool, a two-day sizing validation ramp, and a single-day canary traffic window before full routing.

Key milestones (draft):
- 2027-09-20: Reserved fleet hardware accepted in staging (capacity 48 A100-equivalent GPUs) — infra signoff
- 2027-09-22: Validation day 1 — throughput profiling and KV cache warmup (synth load + 10 customer queries/min baseline)
- 2027-09-23: Validation day 2 — latency SLO runs, spike tests, and model fallback verification
- 2027-09-24: Canary window — 10% production traffic routed to Dedicated, monitoring gating for 4 hours
- 2027-09-25: Full cutover (if canary passes)

Items I need from ACME:
1) Final expected qps distribution by endpoint (chat vs. generation) by Sept 16
2) Network ACLs completed to allow private peering with the fleet (Dan, can you confirm ETA?)
3) Procurement signoff on EULA addendum for reserved capacity (cc'ing procurement@acme.ai)

I attached a compact validation checklist and the fleet config we're proposing. Marcus / Neha / Karthik — please flag anything that needs to move earlier or any gating items we've missed.

Thanks,
Olga

Adding technical detail so we can validate readiness:

Planned fleet config (staging): 6 nodes x 8 A100-eq GPUs = 48 GPUs
Model profile: mix of llama-13b quantized and a trimmed 40B variant for rare endpoints
Memory working set assumptions: 42% prefix reuse across requests; KV cache warmup expected within ~90 minutes of sustained synthetic load

Validation run tasks (ops):
- Day 1: continuous-batch throughput run — measure tokens/sec across 1h windows, assert median token cost +/-10% of forecast
- Day 2: latency p95/p99 sweep with synthetic spikes (burst to 3x baseline) and verify automatic fallback to smaller model variant under memory pressure
- Canary window: health probes every 1 minute, auto rollback trigger if 99p latency increases >10% for 3 consecutive probes or error rate >2%

Network runbook notes: ensure MTU 8900, static routes to the private peering, and firewall rules for gRPC ports 10010-10020. I've attached a minimal runbook (network_runbook.md).

Open questions for the group:
- Do we want the canary to be time-bound (4 hours) or traffic-bound (300k requests)? My vote: traffic-bound with a 6-hour max window.
- Should we pre-warm prefix caches with historical prompt samples from Acme (requires data transfer approval)?

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

Team — acme procurement asked for a clear acceptance gate list so they can prepare contract milestones. Suggest we align technical gates to billing milestones:

Gate A (Staging Acceptance) — when: 2027-09-20
- Fleet available and nodes reachable from Redwood private control plane
- Basic perf sanity: median latency within 20% of hosted baseline

Gate B (Validation Complete) — when: 2027-09-23
- Throughput and latency sweeps completed; KV cache behavior documented
- Post-validation report with token cost delta and recommended quantization profile

Gate C (Canary Approval) — when: 2027-09-24
- Canary monitoring green for 4 hours or traffic-bound threshold met
- Procurement approval to transition billing to reserved capacity

We should provide procurement with the post-validation report template and a short acceptance checklist so they can sign off quickly. Ben — can you own the billing milestone emails and confirm revenue recognition timing?

Karthik
